title: 'Black Box' Revenue From Anthropic and OpenAI Stumps Traders
source_used: Yahoo Finance explainer (citing the Financial Times) and the Newcomer newsletter; the Bloomberg original was not available
key_facts: Bloomberg's headline says revenue figures from Anthropic and OpenAI are a 'black box' that stumps traders.
The Financial Times reported on Thursday 8 Oct 2026 that OpenAI's annualized revenue was approaching $50 billion at the end of September, about $20 billion below the figure it projected last month.

The gap came from OpenAI's backers recalculating its sales to match Anthropic's method, which counts what customers spend on its models through cloud platforms such as Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud, while OpenAI excludes such sales.
Yahoo Finance says the gap does not mean OpenAI missed a target or lost sales; the $70 billion figure was an estimate built on a different way of counting.
Newcomer describes it as a confusion between gross and net revenue, and notes Bloomberg later reported OpenAI expects $70 billion by year-end on the assumption that this is net.
Anthropic reportedly hit $65 billion at the end of July, but the different methods make direct comparison difficult.
Potential Anthropic and OpenAI listings could bring audited accounts into the open.
quote_evidence: According to the FT, the higher number came from OpenAI's backers recalculating its sales to match the method of rival Anthropic, which counts what customers spend on its AI models through cloud platforms such as Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud as revenue, while OpenAI excludes such sales.
On the one hand, it was simply a confusion about gross versus net revenue.
Taken at face value, OpenAI's figure trails the $65 billion (€58bn) Anthropic reportedly hit at the end of July, although the different accounting methods make a direct comparison difficult.
why_it_matters_hint: Investors cannot compare the two leading AI labs because they count revenue differently.
notes: Bloomberg returned a robot check (HTTP 403). Entry built by the desk from Yahoo Finance (Financial Times) and Newcomer, which explain the same confusion; Bloomberg's own findings are therefore not reported beyond its headline.
